standard_prerequisites.name: Koopman operator
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Koopman operator acts on functions by composition with the transformation, and its eigenvalues are the constants for which an eigenfunction exists.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the operator whose eigenvalue minus one is asserted.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induced transformation on a symmetric subinterval
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a suitable symmetric subinterval the induced transformation is again an ergodic symmetric interval exchange transformation, and the centres of its exchanged intervals are images of the centres of the original one.
standard_prerequisites.use: They provide the parity structure used to build the eigenfunction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Rokhlin towers
standard_prerequisites.statement: The induced transformation decomposes the interval into towers of pairwise disjoint intervals of equal height.
standard_prerequisites.use: The eigenfunction is defined level by level on those towers.

core_obligations: Choose a symmetric subinterval that contains no point of any connection, using the disjointness lemma (source line 898).
Use the description of the centres of the induced transformation to conclude that every Rokhlin tower of the induced transformation has even height (source line 899).

Define a function equal to one on the odd levels and to minus one on the even levels of each tower, and check that it is an eigenfunction with eigenvalue minus one for the original transformation (source line 901).

proof_roadmap.step: Select a symmetric subinterval avoiding all connections.
Transfer the parity of the centres to the heights of the Rokhlin towers.
Define the sign function on the levels of the towers and read off the eigenvalue.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled corollary at source lines 893-895: if an ergodic symmetric interval exchange transformation has its middle point inside a connection, then minus one is an eigenvalue of the associated Koopman operator. The proof (source lines 897-902) builds the eigenfunction rather than deducing the eigenvalue abstractly, and every step it needs is outside the statement: a symmetric subinterval avoiding all connections has to be selected, the description of the centres of the induced transformation has to be converted into the statement that all Rokhlin towers have even height, and only then can the level-wise sign function be defined and recognised as an eigenfunction.
